readings_ruling: The dispatch asked five things. (1) No marks. No `**`label`**` appears anywhere in the file; the label sits unmarked at l.11, inside the first 4000 characters. The row is partial, as the REPORT says. (2) Lean ≥ paper for 1°. PremierPrinted (l.609–615) is the printed 1° (l.518–524) exactly. It quantifies over Hausdorff, connected, second-countable V : Type with a projective structure, IsBalayable for all automorphisms, and IsPocheProj P l φ z. Its conclusion is a compatible chart with source univ, EqOn φ' φ P, and P = φ'⁻¹(D ∩ range φ'), which is the same set as φ'⁻¹(D). PremierComposantePrinted (l.599–605) has the same binders and differs only in its last conjunct, ∀ x ∈ P, P = connectedComponentIn (φ'⁻¹ D) x. The general lemmas assume less than the paper (PreconnectedSpace, no T2, no second countability), so Lean ≥ paper for every piece claimed. Reading « sur » as « dans » is forced. In the model, every developing map equal to φ on P is φ, by uniqueness, and its image lies in H₀ ≠ S(n); the audit probe derived range φ̃ ≠ univ from theoreme_premier_model in 6 lines. The statement itself says « sur un ouvert de S(n) ». Benzécri writes « sur » for « dans » elsewhere too: l.156 and l.171 (« la projection de W sur S(n) », for an étalé W) and l.184–185. So this is ordinary usage, at the level of a misprint, and needs no ruling (finding 2). (3) The equivalence. ConnexePrinted (l.620–626) is a fair statement of « D ∩ φ̃(V) connexe ». D ∩ φ̃(V) is an open subset of the affine space H̊, so it is connected by broken lines iff it is connected. Quantifying over every chart φ' instead of the one φ̃ is harmless: the chart exists (exists_chart_poche) and is unique as a map (IsDeveloping.eq_of_eqOn_poche). premierPrinted_iff does not hold by unfolding. It goes through the uniqueness, the open embedding, and the component form (poche_eq_preimage_iff ← poche_eq_connectedComponentIn ← closure_inter_preimage_subset_poche). A brief attempt to settle ConnexePrinted, argued and not formalised, did not settle it. (i) It holds for n ≤ 1. For n = 0, V is a point. For n = 1, a connected open V ⊂ S(1) is an arc or S(1). If its length exceeds π, the star of every M ∈ V (the points joined to M by a segment of V) is an arc longer than π, minus a point, so it cannot lie in the open half-circle H̊ as condition b requires. A pocket therefore forces V to be an arc of length ≤ π inside H̊, and then D ∩ V is an arc. (ii) In every dimension, a counterexample needs φ̃(V) non-convex, since a convex φ̃(V) makes D ∩ φ̃(V) convex. By 3°, P must then be non-convex too, and the cote non-constant (poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero). (iii) Non-convex pockets with a non-constant cote do exist in sweepable manifolds. One is V = ]0,∞[ × (ℝ²∖{0}) ⊂ ℝ³, swept by (t, w) ↦ (at, bw) for a, b > 0 from the compact {1} × {1 ≤ |w| ≤ 2}, with P = ]0,1[ × (ℝ²∖{0}) and z = t. But there P = V ∩ D, so the full form holds. (iv) For a non-constant cote, every segment of V issued from P lies in the open lune H̊ ∩ {z > 0}, by condition b and IsPocheProj.cote_pos_of_ne_zero (Lignes.lean:647). Also ∂_V P ⊂ {z = 1}, by closure_inter_preimage_subset_poche and closure_poche_subset_preimage_hemisphere. So a second component Q would be invisible from P by segments, and reachable from P only by leaving D. No counterexample and no proof was found. The closer's « neither proved nor refuted » stands. The finding was correctly sent to the author as a gap in the printed proof, and the forward reference's « composante connexe » (l.185–186, checked on the scan, p. 248) is proved. (4) The findings. All five are true. Finding 1 (the full form) is statement-level, and the row is partial for it. Findings 2–4 are rightly classed as proof-level, statement unaffected. (2) Condition a says « majorée par 1 » (l.137–138, ≤). The strict z < 1 needed for P ⊆ φ̃⁻¹(D) follows because φ(P) is open and an affine function with an interior maximum is constant, against inf z = 0. The proof of c (l.585–590) argues only the inclusion ⊇. (3) The bracket at l.568–570 is correctly quoted (checked on the scan, p. 254). Transitivity on the fibre gives a γ pointwise; one γ for all of V comes from a's product decomposition and the standing « V connexe ». The finding is true, but it is an elided step rather than an error (finding 4). (4) At l.555–556, « L'assertation a en résulte immédiatement » elides the monodromy (lifting-criterion) argument from « a path over a loop is closed » to a global section. This is true and proof-level. OQ-46: injective_of_isDeveloping_of_poche is stated for every developing map. exemple_poche_projective_of_poche drops `hinj` from the strict exemple_poche_projective under the Theorem's hypotheses only, and its docstring says it decides nothing. That is the dispatch's constraint, met. (5) Build and axioms: see build. (6) Both witnesses instantiate theoreme_premier's hypotheses (see labels). (7) No name clashes. (8) Scope is clean.

labels.notes: Only 1° is in scope (2°–4° belong to T-bz-c2-theoreme), and it is unmarked, as the dispatch asked. Each piece was checked against the transcription l.517–590 and the scan pp. 254–255. 1°, first sentence (l.522–523): exists_chart_poche gives an OpenPartialHomeomorph (open target), IsCompatibleChart (GSR n), source = univ, and EqOn φ' φ P. That is « une carte compatible φ̃ de V sur un ouvert de S(n), induisant φ sur P », in full and under weaker hypotheses (PreconnectedSpace, no T2, no second countability). The chart is unique as a map (IsDeveloping.eq_of_eqOn_poche, which needs only preconnectedness). 1°a (l.538–557): exists_isDeveloping_eqOn_poche is the printed a with « sur » read « dans ». chemin_jets_ferme is the loop step (l.545–556) exactly. jets_produit gives « isomorphe à un produit » as a fibrewise bijection only, disclosed in SCOPE, and that sentence lies inside the proof, not the statement. 1°b (l.559–580): injective_of_isDeveloping_of_poche holds for EVERY developing map, which is stronger than the printed b; with exists_chart_of_injective it makes φ̃ a chart. 1°, second sentence (l.523–524, c at l.582–590): proved in component form (poche_eq_connectedComponentIn, every developing p equal to φ on P, every x ∈ P), and in full for z ≡ 0 (poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero). For a non-constant cote it is reduced, exactly, to the connectedness the proof presumes (poche_eq_preimage_iff, premierPrinted_iff). The REPORT discloses this and marks the row partial. The assembly theoreme_premier carries the chart, the component form and the full-form equivalence. The printed forms are as described in readings_ruling. The forward reference (l.181–186) is situation_exemple, whose conjuncts match the hypotheses of the projective example (l.170–179): a component of φ̃⁻¹(D), inf z = 0 on φ̃(P), and segments from P going into H̊. Non-vacuity: theoreme_premier_model (ℝⁿ, every n, z ≡ 0, P = V) and theoreme_premier_demiDroite (n = 1, P = ]0,1[ ≠ V) both apply theoreme_premier itself to a proved IsBalayable and IsPocheProj. The half-line's cote is non-constant: the audit probe derived ∃ y, z y ≠ 0 from its P ≠ univ through poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero. The statement does not say so explicitly (finding 3).

findings.where: REPORT.json, findings[2] (the γ bracket, l.568–570) and findings[3] (« immédiatement », l.555–556)
findings.what: Both are true and correctly classed as proof-level, statement unaffected. Neither, though, is an error or a missing hypothesis in the DEC-27 sense. « V connexe » is a standing hypothesis of the Theorem. Read with a's product decomposition (J(V) ≅ V × GS(n,ℝ), discrete fibre), the bracket is complete: a continuous section over connected V is a sheet, and the sheets are permuted transitively. The « immédiatement » of a elides the standard monodromy argument.
findings.fix: When forwarding to the author, present them as remarks on elided steps (« the bracket uses a's product structure and V connected without saying so », « immédiatement hides the lifting criterion »), not as gaps.
